posts.meta_description:
2,627 likes, 28 comments - food52 on October 28, 2026: "In French, copain means friend or companion, a word rooted in the idea of sharing bread. It’s a fitting name for Studio CoPain, three French designers who see bread as a way to bring people together. What started as a school project has evolved into a creative studio spanning bread sculptures, hands-on workshops, and food styling. At the heart of it all is a belief in food’s ability to spark conversation and bring people closer together. For a closer look at @studio_co_pain__’s work, comment “story” and we’ll send you the link.

Image 2: Suzanne Craviari
Image 8: @romain__moriceau
Image 10: @billybarraclough".

posts.meta_description:
3,150 likes, 21 comments - food52 on October 26, 2026: "We’re closing out October with a Tasting Notes dedicated to a very special gourd. This week, pumpkin is showing up in all kinds of ways—from soup and cinnamon rolls to candles and ceramic plates. How are you bringing pumpkin into your home this month?

Halloween house: @jessicarchibald takes seasonal decorating very seriously, layering pumpkins across the front of her historic Salt Lake City home.

Black sesame rolls: Swirled pumpkin and black sesame rolls with a black sesame cream cheese frosting, baked by @eatchofood. 

Pumpkin plates: Handmade ceramic pumpkin plates by Italian artist @federica_massimi_ceramics. 

Pumpkin supper: A week of pumpkin and squash soup in an autumn cottage kitchen, by @rosieatthecottage. 

Vintage lanterns: Handmade from cotton, vintage crepe paper, wire, and dyed silk ribbon, each jack-o’-lantern has its own little expression. By @fullmoonwares. 

Pumpkin candles: @ciergeriedespremontres turns plump pumpkins and speckled squash into wax candles. 

Pastry of the week: Pumpkin cheesecake with miso caramel sauce, from Amsterdam culinary studio and shop, @oficina.amsterdam. 

Pumpkin patch: More than 130 varieties of heirloom and specialty pumpkins, all handpicked at @gordonskagitfarms. 

Pumpkin crullers: @thainybites’s filled pumpkin crullers, fresh in the Test Kitchen. Recipe (and video) coming soon!".

posts.meta_description:
2,817 likes, 303 comments - food52 on October 23, 2026: "Before you toss those apple peels and cores, turn them into homemade jelly. Apples are naturally rich in pectin, which helps the jelly set when combined with sugar and acid at the right temperature. All it takes is boiling and reducing (ours took about 50 minutes) to turn leftover scraps into a delicious spread for toast, pancakes, cheese boards, and more.
Comment "apple" for the full recipe!".
